sections.title: 1. What Ostrevia is and what it is used for

blocks.text: Ostrevia contains the active substance lumiravostat. It works by calming the part of the immune system that causes inflammation of the skin.
Ostrevia is used to treat adults with long-lasting (chronic) hand eczema that is moderate to severe, when strong steroid creams have not worked well enough or cannot be used.

sections.title: 2. What you need to know before you take Ostrevia

items: if you are allergic to lumiravostat or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6)
if you have active tuberculosis (TB) or another serious infection
if you are pregnant

blocks.text: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Ostrevia if you:

items: have an infection, or keep getting infections. Ostrevia can lower your body’s ability to fight infections.
have had TB or been in close contact with someone with TB. Your doctor will test you for TB before you start.
have had cancer, or get new skin growths
have had blood clots in your legs or lungs
have liver problems

blocks.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you get a fever, chills, cough, leg pain or swelling, chest pain or sudden shortness of breath.
You will have blood tests before you start and while you take Ostrevia.
Do not give this medicine to children and adolescents under 18 years because it has not been studied in this age group.

Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking, have recently taken or might take any other medicines, especially medicines for fungal infections (such as ketoconazole) or tuberculosis (such as rifampicin).
Do not take Ostrevia if you are pregnant. It may harm your unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective contraception while taking Ostrevia and for 4 weeks after your last dose.
Do not breast-feed while taking Ostrevia and for 4 days after your last dose.
Ostrevia is not expected to affect your ability to drive or use machines.
This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, that is to say essentially ‘sodium-free’.
Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. Check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure.
The recommended dose is one 10 mg tablet once a day. Your doctor may increase it to one 25 mg tablet once a day after 12 weeks. Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food.

subs.title: If you take more Ostrevia than you should

blocks.text: Talk to a doctor or pharmacist straight away.

subs.title: If you forget to take Ostrevia

blocks.text: Take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten tablet.
Talk to your doctor before you stop. Your eczema may come back.
If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor or pharmacist.
Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.

Serious side effects. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice: signs of a serious infection (fever, chills, cough, burning when passing urine); signs of a blood clot (leg pain or swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath).
Very common (may affect more than 1 in 10 people): common cold.
Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people): headache, feeling sick (nausea), acne, shingles (herpes zoster), changes in blood tests.
Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people): pneumonia, skin infection (cellulitis), blood clots in the legs or lungs.

If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.
Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the carton and blister after EXP. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.
Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.

subs.title: Special warnings and precautions for use

blocks.text: Serious infections: serious and sometimes fatal infections, including pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported. Ostrevia should be interrupted if a patient develops a serious infection until the infection is controlled. Vaccination against herpes zoster should be considered before starting treatment.
Malignancy: malignancies, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, have been observed. Periodic skin examination is recommended.

Venous thromboembolism: deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported. Ostrevia should be used with caution in patients with risk factors for venous thromboembolism and discontinued promptly if symptoms occur.
Laboratory abnormalities: lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes should be monitored at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months thereafter.
Excipients: This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, that is to say essentially ‘sodium-free’.

subs.title: Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

blocks.text: Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole) increase exposure; the dose should be 10 mg once daily. Strong CYP3A4 inducers (for example rifampicin) decrease exposure and may reduce efficacy; concomitant use is not recommended.
Women of childbearing potential: effective contraception should be used during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
Pregnancy: there are no data from the use of lumiravostat in pregnant women. Studies in animals have shown reproductive toxicity (see section 5.3). Ostrevia is contraindicated during pregnancy.
Breast-feeding: lumiravostat is excreted in the milk of rats. A risk to the breast-fed child cannot be excluded. Ostrevia should not be used during breast-feeding and for 4 days after the last dose.
Fertility: no effect on fertility was seen in animal studies.

subs.title: Effects on ability to drive and use machines

blocks.text: Ostrevia has no or negligible influence on the ability to drive and use machines.
Summary of the safety profile: the most common adverse reactions were nasopharyngitis (12%), headache (9%), nausea (7%) and acne (6%).

Reporting suspected adverse reactions after authorisation of the medicinal product is important. It allows continued monitoring of the benefit/risk balance of the medicinal product. There is no specific antidote. In case of overdose, the patient should be monitored for signs and symptoms of adverse reactions and supportive treatment given. Haemodialysis is not expected to remove lumiravostat.
Pharmacotherapeutic group: immunosuppressants, ATC code: not yet assigned.
Mechanism of action: lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase.

notice.title: PRAC recommendation on a signal: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
notice.text: Having reviewed the available evidence, PRAC agreed that the marketing authorisation holder(s) of lumiravostat-containing products should submit a variation within 60 days to amend the product information as follows. SmPC section 4.4: "Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), which can be life-threatening or fatal, has been reported. Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions. If signs and symptoms suggestive of DRESS appear, Ostrevia should be withdrawn immediately." SmPC section 4.8, Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, frequency not known: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Package leaflet section 2 (Warnings and precautions) and section 4: a widespread rash, high body temperature and enlarged lymph nodes (DRESS or drug hypersensitivity syndrome): stop taking Ostrevia and contact your doctor or seek medical attention immediately.
